summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after a witnessed seizure, with associated fever, leukocytosis, and hypotension. Evaluation revealed left lower lobe pneumonia and a bloodstream infection with coagulase-negative staphylococcus, likely central-line associated. She was treated with IV antibiotics, and her PICC line was removed. Neurology recommended increasing levetiracetam to 1000 mg twice daily. Nutrition transitioned her from a bariatric stage 3 diet to a diabetic carb-consistent diet with six small meals and Glucerna supplementation to manage post-prandial hypoglycemia and support caloric intake. She gradually tolerated oral intake with intermittent pain managed by scheduled and breakthrough analgesia. Repeat blood cultures cleared, and she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable. She was discharged home with follow-up planned in neurology, endocrinology, and nutrition, along with outpatient lab testing for insulin and C-peptide.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter, initial encounter
Sepsis due to Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
